title: Fino1: On the Transferability of Reasoning-Enhanced LLMs and Reinforcement Learning to Finance

task.value: Improving and evaluating LLMs' financial reasoning (numerical QA over financial texts, tables, long documents and equations) via a CoT corpus, SFT+RL-trained models, and a benchmark.
task.quote: To address these gaps, we introduce FinCoT, the first open high-fidelity CoT corpus for finance, distilled from seven QA datasets by a novel three-stage pipeline that incorporates domain supervision, iterative LLM refinement, and difficulty-aware filtering.

architecture.value: Three-stage CoT construction (GPT-4o synthesis with domain guidance, GPT-4o generator/verifier iterative refinement, Llama3.1-8B difficulty filtering), then two-stage training of Qwen3: SFT on FinCoT_SFT then RL (PPO, DPO, GRPO) with GPT-4o-judged multi-part reward.
architecture.quote: Following previous studies [1, 8], a two-stage training approach, supervised fine-tuning and RL, is adopted to develop the model. FinCoT is divided into two parts FinCoT_SFT (7686) and FinCoT_RL (1,500) to support the training.

data.value: FinCoT: 9,186 CoT-annotated QA pairs from FinQA, ConvFinQA, DocFinQA, TATQA, Econ_Logic, DocMath-Eval, BizBench-QA; evaluated on FinReason (FinQA 1,100, DM-Simplong 100, DM-Complong 300, XBRL-Math 90) from financial reports and XBRL filings.
data.quote: Building our raw data collection, we further curate the first dataset containing 9,186 chain-of-thought annotated QA pairs, specifically designed to support SFT and RL for financial reasoning models

window.value: No dated period; FinCoT split into 7,686 SFT and 1,500 RL examples; evaluation on separate FinReason benchmark datasets.
window.quote: FinCoT is divided into two parts FinCoT_SFT (7686) and FinCoT_RL (1,500) to support the training.

models.value: Backbones Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B (Fin-o1-8B, Fin-o1-14B); GPT-4o used for CoT generation, verification and reward judging; Llama3.1-8B-Instruct for difficulty filtering.
models.quote: Qwen3 are selected as backbone models, given their strong performance among small and mid-sized LLMs (shown in Table 3).

baselines.value: 29 LLMs including GPT-4o, GPT-o1-preview, GPT-o3-mini, GPT-4.5, DeepSeek-V3/R1, Llama and Qwen families, R1-distills, S1-32B, Limo, FinR1-7B, Dianjin-R1-7B; plus ablations with PPO, DPO, no-CoT SFT.
baselines.quote: we select a diverse set of 29 LLMs from the GPT, LLaMA, DeepSeek, and Qwen families, along with other reasoning models including both general domain and financial specific models.

headline_result.value: Fin-o1-14B average accuracy 61.07 across four FinReason datasets, second only to DeepSeek-V3 (61.30); Fin-o1-8B averages 59.95.

limitations.value: Limited model scale, restricted evaluation scope, reliance on a single dataset (FinQA) for reasoning path construction, and a single path-generation method (GPT-4o); not suitable for real-world financial use.
limitations.quote: Fourth, our reasoning path construction approach is simplified, as we generate paths using a single method (GPT-4o), whereas exploring multiple reasoning path generation strategies—such as ensemble approaches or human-annotated paths—could lead to more robust financial reasoning capabilities.

release.value: Datasets, models and code released on Hugging Face (TheFinAI/FinCoT, Fin-o1-8B, Fin-o1-14B) and GitHub (The-FinAI/Fino1).
